archetype.name: Contender That Fell Short (run prevention first)
archetype.definition: A 100-win division champion with the league's stingiest run prevention and an A-graded lineup, whose offense disappeared in October and was swept out of the NLCS.

report.headline: Best run prevention in baseball, 100 wins, then an NLCS sweep with silent bats

recap.finish: 100-62, won the NL West; beat ATL 3-1 in the NLDS, swept 0-4 by MIL in the NLCS
recap.body:
This was the most complete Dodgers regular season since 2022. They allowed 3.7 runs a game, the fewest in the league and 0.78 below the league rate, and scored enough to rank fourth in offense with the second-best team OPS (.762). The Run Diff / G of 1.24 ranked second. The 100 wins were not built on luck either: the margin implied 101.9, so a W vs Run Diff of -1.9 means they slightly underperformed their runs. All three roster groups graded in the A range: hitters A, rotation A-, bullpen A-.

The shape of the year was a strong first half, a lull in midsummer and a hard finish. The Dodgers were 56-30 at the end of June after winning every month by a wide margin. Then July (13-11) and August (13-14) turned flat. In both months they were outscored, and August's offense managed just 3.85 runs a game. September brought an 18-7 month, and the regular season closed 8-2 with only 2.2 runs allowed a game over the last ten. One warning sign was there: in the final five games the lineup scored just 2.8 a game.

The pitching is the real change from recent years. After two straight seasons ranked 13th in run prevention with ERAs near 3.9, the staff posted a 3.55 ERA and ranked first in run prevention, which it last did in 2022. Tarik Skubal (5.2 WAR, 2.51 FIP) and Yoshinobu Yamamoto (4.7 WAR, 2.53 ERA) gave the rotation two aces. Tanner Scott's 2.09 FIP and 25 saves anchored a bullpen whose top arms all held ERAs under 3.25 apart from Kyle Hurt. The lineup's value was spread out. Andy Pages led with 4.5 WAR and 8.4 Def Runs, Max Muncy hit 29 homers with a 129 wRC+, and Shohei Ohtani's 139 wRC+ was the best on the club.

October split in two. The NLDS against Atlanta went 3-1, won by pitching: Atlanta never scored more than three runs. Against Milwaukee the bats went dark. The Dodgers lost a 2-1 opener and never scored more than four runs in any game of the sweep. The postseason OPS of .590 ranked ninth of 12 playoff teams, and the team scored 3.13 runs a game. Will Smith (-27 wRC+), Tommy Edman (-42), Freddie Freeman (68) and Mookie Betts (70) all went cold together. Kyle Tucker, the weakest regular bat in the summer, was the only hitter who carried over (163 wRC+).

That leaves a curious ledger. The regular season was better than either of the last two, which ended with 11 and 13 playoff wins. This one ended with three. Eight games of slumping hitters say far less about the roster than 162 games of the league's best run prevention.

highlights.title: League's best run prevention returns
highlights.body: The Dodgers allowed the fewest runs a game in the league and cut their team ERA well below last year's, reversing two seasons ranked 13th in run prevention. The cause is mostly two starters at the top plus a deep, strikeout-heavy bullpen rather than defense, since Fielding Runs ranked only 11th. It looks sustainable as long as the top of the staff stays intact.

highlights.title: Skubal and Yamamoto as co-aces
highlights.body: Skubal's 2.51 FIP backs up his 2.72 ERA, which makes him the most trustworthy arm on the staff. Yamamoto's 2.53 ERA ran ahead of a 3.33 FIP, so some of his run prevention was batted-ball fortune, though a 0.87 WHIP is no fluke. Both also held up in October.

highlights.title: Deep lineup led by Pages
highlights.body: The hitters earned an A grade without relying on one star. Pages paired a 123 wRC+ with plus defense for 4.5 WAR, Muncy produced a 129 wRC+, and Ohtani's 139 led the club. Four regulars rank in the top ten at their positions on the site.

lowlights.title: Offense vanished in the NLCS
lowlights.body: A lineup with the league's second-best OPS hit .590 in October, and the NLCS was lost in four straight with never more than four runs a game. The collapse was broad: Smith, Edman, Freeman and Betts all finished far below average, Smith at a -27 wRC+. It is an eight-game sample and mostly says hitters slumped together at the wrong moment, not that the lineup is broken.

lowlights.title: Midsummer stall
lowlights.body: After a 56-30 start, the Dodgers played roughly .500 ball in July and August and were outscored in both months. The offense sagged to 3.85 runs a game in August while the pitching gave back its early-season edge. The strong September shows the slide was not permanent, but it is the stretch that kept this from being a 2022-level year.

lowlights.title: Soft spots: Tucker and the back end
lowlights.body: Tucker logged the second-most plate appearances on the team yet produced a league-average 100 wRC+ and -5 Def Runs, ranking 75th of 182 outfielders. Roki Sasaki and Emmet Sheehan both posted ERAs above 4.4 over more than 110 innings each, worse than the league average.

arc.note: Dominant through June at 56-30, roughly break-even and outscored in July and August, then an 18-7 September. A 3-1 NLDS win gave way to an NLCS sweep.

recap.nextYear: The foundation is the pitching. Skubal's peripherals say his season was real, Yamamoto's say expect a slightly higher ERA, and Scott's 2.09 FIP makes the closer role secure. The lineup's core of Pages, Muncy, Ohtani and Betts produced the bulk of the hitting WAR. Freeman's .430 slugging is modest for a first baseman, and Tucker's average production at heavy playing time is the clearest place to upgrade. The back of the rotation behind the top three needs better run prevention. Little of the 100 wins was luck: the W vs Run Diff was slightly negative for the second straight year. The October offensive collapse rests on eight games and shouldn't outweigh a full season in which this club ranked second in Run Diff / G.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; postseason judgments rest on only eight games.
